title: Edo Japan's Daredevil Firefighters
hook: Firefighter brigades competed to climb burning roofs waving giant paper standards.

scenes.text: Because the metropolis of Edo was built almost entirely of cedar timber and paper screens, fires spread like wildfire.
scenes.imagePrompt: Tightly packed Edo period city street with wooden two-story merchant houses and tiled watchtowers under dramatic sky. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Because the metropolis of Edo was built almost entirely of cedar timber and paper screens, fires spread like wildfire.

scenes.text: Conflagrations were nicknamed 'the flowers of Edo', striking so often that the Shogun established forty-eight neighborhood firefighter brigades.
scenes.imagePrompt: Tall wooden fire watchtower in Edo with brass alarm bell and hemp pull-rope overlooking sprawling tile rooftops. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Conflagrations were nicknamed 'the flowers of Edo', striking so often that the Shogun established forty-eight neighborhood firefighter brigades.

scenes.text: Firefighters were working-class heroes called 'hikeshi', famous for their full-body dragon tattoos and heavy quilted indigo coats soaked in water.
scenes.imagePrompt: Heavy indigo-dyed cotton firefighter coat sashiko-stitched with geometric patterns and water crest symbols on a wooden hanger. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Firefighters were working-class heroes called 'hikeshi', famous for their full-body dragon tattoos and heavy quilted indigo coats soaked in water.

scenes.text: Their job wasn't putting out flames with water, but tearing down neighboring houses with long iron-hooked poles called 'tobiguchi' to create firebreaks.
scenes.imagePrompt: Iron-hooked wooden firefighter pry poles, timber saws, and wooden water buckets resting beside charred building beams. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Their job wasn't putting out flames with water, but tearing down neighboring houses with long iron-hooked poles called 'tobiguchi' to create firebreaks.

scenes.text: Daredevils scaled collapsing burning roofs to plant their brigade's 'matoi' standard—a heavy paper and wood banner—claiming honor for their squad.
